exposure: Maternal health status (healthy pregnancy, maternal diabetes, hypertensive disease, maternal diabetes and hypertensive disease, psychological disorders/diseases, psychological diseases with either diabetes or hypertension)
outcome: Postpartum hospital readmissions for women and infants
cohort: The study included 130,533 singleton term pregnancies of women living in the South-West Sydney Local Health District between January 1st, 2001, and December 31st, 2016.
finding: Women with complicated pregnancies in South-West Sydney Local Health District experienced significantly more adverse obstetric and child outcomes, along with increased hospital readmissions for both mothers and infants within the first year postpartum.
mod_finding: Women with complex pregnancies were more likely to have an induction of labour, epidural anaesthesia, and caesarean section compared to women with healthy pregnancies.
